newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banks profits better than expected - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Thai banks profits better than expected - analysts.

text.p: Most major Thai banks reported better-than-expected profits in the first quarter of this year despite substantially increasing provisions for non-performing loans during the period, analysts said on Tuesday.

"The results are not as bad as we had expected. We previously projected the (banking) industry to post a bigger decline in earnings in the quarter," said Thanita Leelahawan, banking analyst at Multi Credit Corp of Thailand.

Among the major commercial banks, the second-largest Krung Thai Bank Plc on Tuesday posted a 24 percent drop in the first quarter net profit to 2.5 billion baht ($96 million) from 3.27 billion in the same period last year.
Thai Farmers Bank Plc announced a first quarter profit of 2.65 billion baht, down from 3.01 billion in the same quarter a year ago.
The Thai stock market took the bank results in stride and did not fall as much as had been expected, brokers said. Then SET index was down 0.44 percent at 691.16 points at 1010 GMT.
Analysts said they had expected most banks to announce lower profits in the quarter because the nation's sluggish economy was hampering banks' interest and other income.
The slowing economy and related woes in businesses had also prompted them to raise provisions for non-performing loans.

Thanita at MCC said she expected the banking industry to post negative earnings growth of nine percent in the first quarter, while the results of all banks so far posted only two percent negative growth.

"Banks' interest and other revenues were in line with the overall economic conditions. The rise in provision for non-performing loans also affected their profit," said an analyst at Capital Nomura Securities.

Analysts said the prolonged slump in the property sector, which has shown no sign of recovering, would continue to hit banks' earnings in the future as some cash-strapped property developers failed to repay their loans.

"It's going to get worse for bank and finance companies as the proportion of non-performing loans rises. Some property companies have problems paying off their existing loans," said Philip Sheridan, analyst at Thaimex Finance and Securities.

In a major shake up of the troubled financial sector, Thai authorities last month ordered banks to raise provisions for sub-standard assets, mainly in the form of billions of dollars in bad loans to the depressed property sector.
Bangkok Bank Plc, the biggest commercial bank, on Monday reported a first quarter result of 5.03 billion baht compared with 4.52 billion in the same quarter in 1996.
"Bangkok Bank had doubled the amount of provisions for non-performing loans in the quarter. This significantly affected its earnings in the quarter," said the Capital Nomura analyst.

Analysts had expected Bangkok Bank to post a higher profit. They said if Bangkok Bank had set aside the same amount of provisions for non-performing loans as in the same quarter last year, the bank's profit for the first quarter of 1997 would have increased more than 15 percent, compared with the 11 percent announced.
Another major bank Siam Commercial Bank Plc posted earnings of 2.23 billion baht in the quarter compared with 2.04 billion in the same period a year ago.
